heroHeadline: NDB Backs $1B South Africa Infrastructure Push as Transport Ministers Meet in Nagpur Ahead of Sept Summit
heroSubtitle: The New Development Bank approved up to $1 billion on June 17 for urban infrastructure across eight South African metros, its largest single-country commitment since the May Moscow Annual Meeting confirmed $42.9B in cumulative approvals. BRICS transport ministers adopted a joint declaration in Nagpur on July 11, covering logistics resilience, decarbonisation, and a new BRICS Railway Research Network, followed by an expert-level connectivity conference in Moscow on July 13. India's chairmanship continues building toward the September 12-13 New Delhi summit, where BRICS Pay — linking SPFS, CIPS, UPI, and Pix payment rails — is targeted for operational launch and a further round of accession decisions is anticipated. IMF's July WEO Update confirms BRICS's 2026 growth advantage over the G7 holds at 2.6 percentage points, even as Saudi Arabia's membership remains unresolved and the bloc still processes fallout from May's FM Meeting breakdown.
footerNote: Data sourced from official BRICS declarations, NDB annual reports, IMF, UNCTAD, and major international outlets. Source tiers reflect editorial confidence levels.
